subject: french
title: Stamp 3: Banlieues and Citizenship
welcome_lead: Stamp the realities of banlieues and the question of citizenship.
meta_desc: A-Level French adventure on the banlieues, integration debates, and French citizenship.

concepts.def: Suburb; in French debates, often refers to disadvantaged outer-city housing estates.
Housing projects on the outskirts of cities, often associated with social problems.
Three weeks of riots starting October 2005 in Clichy-sous-Bois after two teenagers died.
Integration: the process by which immigrants and descendants become part of French society.
Citizenship; acquired by birth on French soil (with conditions) or naturalisation.
The 'French melting pot' model, contrasted with multiculturalist approaches.

walkthroughs.body_html: On 27 October 2005, Zyed Benna and Bouna Traore died fleeing police in Clichy-sous-Bois. Riots spread across 274 communes. Sarkozy, then interior minister, called rioters racaille, fuelling controversy.
France traditionally rejects American-style multiculturalism in favour of universalism: citizens are individuals, not members of ethnic groups. Critics argue this masks structural discrimination.
French citizenship can be acquired by droit du sol (born on French soil, with conditions), droit du sang (one parent French), marriage, or naturalisation (typically after 5 years of residence).
